advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the per-ticket full-log fold in `snapshot-close-metadata` so a converged store does not re-run the expensive double-reduce on every init/MCP-boot sweep (e.g. a persisted converged marker or a cheaper selection prefilter), given it holds the write lock and scales with store size.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/snapshot_ensures.py:54-55 — `replayed = reduce_ticket(ticket_dir)` and `full = fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state(ticket_id, ticket_dir)` run per candidate ticket inside the scan loop (lines 67-77)
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:633 — `state = reduce_ticket(ticket_dir, include_retired=True)` folds the entire active+retired log, so cost scales with the ticket's event history

src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:163-166 — `for uid in REGISTRY_IDS: fn = reg[uid]; outcomes.append(fn(tracker))` runs every unit unconditionally under `write_lock`; the `.ensure-applied` marker (via `_pending_ids`, line 197-205) only drives the read-only hint, so a converged sweep still executes the full per-ticket fold

docs/migrations.md:108-114 — author-measured: a converged sweep 'still costs about 21.5 s under the lock, because it re-checks every reopened ticket that carries close metadata' and the sweep 'holds the write lock for that whole time, so other writers wait behind it'; runs at `init`, `fsck --repair` and MCP boot
advisory.finding: The `snapshot-close-metadata` ensure unit performs a full-log fold per candidate ticket (`reduce_ticket` plus `fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state`, which re-reduces the entire active+retired event log) on every sweep, including converged stores, and this sweep runs under the write lock on every MCP boot. Because `run_ensures` executes all registry units unconditionally (the `.ensure-applied` marker gates only the read-only hint, not the sweep body), the cost recurs on each boot/init and scales with the number of reopened tickets carrying close metadata times each ticket's event-history length.
scenarios: Large store with many reopened tickets carrying close metadata: every MCP boot / init re-runs the full double-fold scan under the write lock, adding tens of seconds of boot latency and blocking concurrent writers for that duration
Store growth: both the candidate count and each ticket's full-log fold length increase, so the converged-sweep cost degrades super-linearly with store size
